source.objectiveEnglish: Ask what, who, where, when, how many and why about tasks, plans and permits on site.
source.focusSpanish: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál
source.speakingEnglish: Ask a crew member where the blueprints are, who has the permit, and when the inspector is coming.

archivedDraft.title: Correct the tool name
archivedDraft.scene: In storage, Sato holds his saw and new helper Kobayashi holds Sato's hammer; after Kobayashi checks the saw's name, Sato quizzes him about the hammer before they put the tools away
materialDrift: Old Japanese Foundation 7 names Sato and Kobayashi's saw and hammer in a storage-room yes/no exercise; current source asks Luis and Rosa site, blueprint, permit, inspection and worker-count questions.

cards.sourceNoteInternal: Two words with an accent for 'why'; porque, one word, means 'because'.

cards.japaneseDraft: 図面はどこにありますか。
今日は誰がフォークリフトを運転しますか。
検査員はいつ来ますか。

cards.sourceEnglish: How many boards are we missing?
cards.japaneseDraft: 板は何枚足りませんか。

cards.sourceNoteInternal: Before a noun, ¿qué? is the standard choice. You may hear ¿cuál escalera? in Mexico.
cards.japaneseDraft: どのはしごを使いますか。

reader.sourceSpanish: En la obra, Luis le pregunta a Rosa: ¿Dónde están los planos?
reader.sourceEnglish: At the site, Luis asks Rosa: Where are the blueprints?
reader.japaneseDraft: 現場でルイスはローサに尋ねます。「図面はどこにありますか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Están en la troca, pero ¿qué plano necesita usted?
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: They are in the truck, but which blueprint do you need?
reader.japaneseDraft: ローサ：「トラックの中にあります。でも、どの図面が必要ですか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Necesito el plano de la cocina, y ¿quién tiene el permiso?
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: I need the kitchen blueprint, and who has the permit?
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「台所の図面が必要です。それと、許可証は誰が持っていますか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Yo tengo el permiso, pero ¿por qué lo necesita?
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: I have the permit, but why do you need it?
reader.japaneseDraft: ローサ：「私が許可証を持っています。でも、なぜ必要なのですか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Hay inspección hoy, pero ¿cuándo viene el inspector?
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: There is an inspection today, but when is the inspector coming?
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「今日は検査があります。でも、検査員はいつ来ますか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Viene a las 10, según la oficina, pero ¿qué revisa?
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: He comes at 10, according to the office, but what does he check?
reader.japaneseDraft: ローサ：「事務所によると10時に来ます。でも、何を調べますか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Revisa la cocina, pero ¿cuántos trabajadores hay allí?
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: He checks the kitchen, but how many workers are there?
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「台所を調べます。でも、そこには作業員が何人いますか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Hay 4 trabajadores, y ¿cuánto tiempo necesita el inspector?
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: There are 4 workers, and how much time does the inspector need?
reader.japaneseDraft: ローサ：「作業員は4人います。それと、検査員にはどのくらい時間が必要ですか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis: Una hora, más o menos, pero ¿cómo está la cocina ahora?
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis: About one hour, but how does the kitchen look now?
reader.japaneseDraft: ルイス：「だいたい1時間です。でも、台所は今どんな状態ですか。」

decisionsNeeded: Resolve source cuánto amount-versus-duration and cuántos noun/classifier senses before selecting Japanese cards 5 and 6.
Resolve cuál as stand-alone which versus qué before a noun; source card 16 asks which ladder with qué, so Japanese どの is only a contextual candidate.
Identify what kind of site permit the source means before selecting card 10 and Reader 3–4 Japanese 許可証 terminology; do not invent a permit type or legal requirement.
Confirm the site inspection/blueprint/truck/kitchen scene, characters, ten-o'clock visit, four-worker count and approximately one-hour duration with qualified Japanese and construction reviewers.
Review polite register for Spanish usted, forklift operator wording and the source question-words objective as Japanese curriculum, not a Spanish-word translation exercise.
Author exact six mode prompt/target pairs, forms, speaking, contextual dictionary and saved-item mapping; verify exact text before audio synthesis and distinct listening review.
